meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone hear Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you actually have on the essay.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He wrote it over the weekend, somewhere else, and pasted it in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Then hear this. Whatever comes of that page, nothing goes on his record, and none of it gets talked about in front of his class.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
So he misremembered a line from Hamlet. Half your class must do that.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Not close to anything. Then say what you're asking of him, Hale.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Kids change their argument in two weeks. And you still haven't told me what you want from him.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Then he'll do it, to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, before December 1, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record. All of that in my inbox tonight, Hale.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
He works shifts at the grocery store. I'll confirm Thursday tonight, when I answer your email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school, not in front of Owen's class, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require that agreement from you in writing, including the proposed date of Thursday the twelfth. I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite. She still wants your written confirmation tonight, the new mark to replace the zero, and nothing on his record. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times and then answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by inviting a dated draft, and she trusts dated records she can check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you ground; the closest was leaving her question about what you wanted from Owen unanswered while you laid out the outline, which made her sharper.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history placed the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on a Wednesday night in late October, which came very close to that memory. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked what you were asking of Owen, name procedure 4.4 right then instead of adding the outline, so she doesn't have to ask twice.
